ille, illa, illud

demonstrative pronoun and adjective; genitive illīus, dative illī · Declension on Wiktionary

that; (plural) those

What is away from both speaker and listener, in place or in time; with hic, “this … that”. The neuter often points ahead to what follows: illud mīror, “one thing surprises me”. After a name it marks someone famous (see “the”).

Other words

  • iste, ista, istud — that (by you, of yours)

    demonstrative pronoun and adjective · also used · classical · Catull. 10.25–26: paulum istōs commodā; Mart. 4.49.10: laudant illa, sed ista legunt · Declension on Wiktionary

    The demonstrative of the person spoken to: what is near you or yours, or what you are talking about (Lewis & Short). Hence the adverbs istīc, istūc, istinc, there where you are.

  • is, ea, id — that, the one (just mentioned)

    demonstrative pronoun, unemphatic · also used · classical · Cic. Amic. 80: est enim is quī est tamquam alter īdem; Ter. Ad. 978: Ob eam rem? — Ob eam. · Declension on Wiktionary

    The weak “that”: it points back to what has been named, and stands before a relative: is quī, the one who; id quod, that which, what.

Examples

  • phasēlus ille, quem vidētis, hospitēs, ait fuisse nāvium celerrimus

    that boat you see, my guests, says she was once the fastest of shipsCatull. 4.1–2

  • cōnfiteor: laudant illa, sed ista legunt

    I admit it: they praise those, but they read theseMart. 4.49.10

  • ille terrārum mihi praeter omnīs angulus rīdet

    that corner of the earth smiles on me above all othersHor. C. 2.6.13–14

  • cētera bellē; illud mīror

    everything else is fine; one thing surprises meCic. Fam. 7.18.2

  • quaesō … mihi, mī Catulle, paulum istōs commodā

    please, my Catullus, lend me those men of yours for a little whileCatull. 10.25–26

  • est enim is quī est tamquam alter īdem

    for a friend is one who is, as it were, a second selfCic. Amic. 80

See also this, the, there, this one or that one?.
